newsitem.title: USA: Southern Pacific cites Q1 strength for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Southern Pacific cites Q1 strength for 1997.

text.p: Southern Pacific Funding Corp said Tuesday it saw strength in its first quarter as indicative of its prospects 1997.
"We believe that the first quarter strength is indicative of the Company's prospects for the balance of 1997 and future years," said president and chief executive Robert Howard.

"Our current cash position is strong. Our strategy continues to focus on developing low-cost loan origination channels that have lower capital requirements. Our cash position provides us with the capital to sustain current loan production near-term. In addition, during the quarter we initiated whole loan sales of conforming and second mortgage product that generated cash for the Company." he continued.
Net income for the quarter ended March 31, 1997 increased 188.2 percent to a record $12.6 million, compared with $4.4 million for the quarter ended March 31, 1996.

"The first quarter results confirm our confidence in the strength of the non-conforming home equity loan market, and SPFC's ability to increase loan production while managing infrastructure growth," said Howard. "Demand for our product is healthy as evidenced by continuing expansion of existing and new production channels."
